kf: **Photoageing** is premature skin ageing from chronic UV (and visible/infrared) exposure, on top of intrinsic ageing.
Wrinkles, coarse texture, mottled pigment, solar lentigines, telangiectasia, yellowish thickening (**solar elastosis**).
Marks cumulative sun damage and higher risk of AK, BCC, SCC and melanoma: examine the skin.
Prevention: sun protection and stopping smoking; topical **retinoids** have the best evidence for treatment.
Procedures (peels, lasers, injectables) are cosmetic and not NHS-funded.

sub: Fair skin, outdoor workers, sunbed users, sunny climates; smoking adds damage.

aet: UVA penetrates the dermis (collagen and elastin damage); UVB damages the epidermis and DNA.
myths: **"A tan protects the skin"**: a tan is a sign of DNA damage.
**"Anti-ageing creams reverse wrinkles"**: only retinoids and sun protection have good evidence.
patho_lead: UV turns on **collagen-destroying enzymes** while slowing new collagen formation.

mech.t: UV generates reactive oxygen species in skin cells.
Signalling (AP-1) switches on matrix metalloproteinases that digest collagen.
New collagen synthesis falls; fragmented collagen weakens the dermis: wrinkles.
Abnormal elastic material builds up in the upper dermis, causing yellow, thickened skin.
Uneven melanocyte activity (lentigines) and dilated vessels (telangiectasia) appear.

histo: Solar elastosis (blue-grey amorphous elastic material in the papillary dermis), reduced collagen, atrophic or uneven epidermis.

sub: Photoageing appears later and is mainly pigmentary (uneven tone, dermatosis papulosa nigra) rather than wrinkles.

comp: Actinic keratoses and skin cancers; skin fragility, purpura and skin tears.
prog: Partly preventable and partly reversible with photoprotection and retinoids.
